change_notes: Seed record compiled 2026-06-07 from Apex's official help-center pages (apextraderfunding.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch in the research environment; facts drawn from search-engine-indexed snippets of those pages plus cross-checked third-party trackers — see source_url). Marked 'draft' pending a human operator confirming every field firsthand on apextraderfunding.com. Reflects the post-'Apex 4.0' ruleset that took effect around 2026-03-01 — pre-2026-03-01 ('Legacy') accounts ran a different consistency-rule formula and payout structure; do not use this record for an 'as of' query before that date. Apex also sells an Intraday Trailing Drawdown evaluation variant at the same sizes with different drawdown params; that variant is not yet captured as a separate lineage.

lock.notes: Apex's own materials describe the lock level as 'starting balance + $100' (e.g. $50,100 on a $50K account) rather than exactly the starting balance — locked_level reflects that $100 offset, it is not a rounding artifact.

drawdown.notes: Recalculated once per trading day at 4:59:59 PM ET off the END-OF-DAY (closing/realized) balance — intraday unrealized swings do not move the floor mid-session, but the resulting threshold is enforced in real time the instant balance touches it. The $2,500 amount is carried over from a pre-4.0 published table; Apex's exact post-4.0 EOD-variant figure for $50K should be re-checked directly against the live size/drawdown chart before this record is marked 'verified'.

consistency_rule.basis_definition: Apex applies no best-day/consistency cap during the Evaluation phase — by the firm's own description an evaluation 'can be passed in a single session,' which a meaningful consistency constraint would make impossible.

targets_and_days.notes: Apex explicitly imposes NO minimum-trading-day requirement to pass an evaluation — reaching the profit target without breaching the drawdown is sufficient even on day one. This is a real point of divergence from Take Profit Trader (5-day minimum) and Tradeify's Select track (3-day minimum), both of which gate evaluation passes on a minimum day count to backstop their consistency rules.

payout.eligibility_notes: Evaluation accounts cannot request payouts. Passing converts the account into a funded Performance Account (PA) — see this lineage's 'funded' record for PA payout terms — which itself requires a one-time PA activation fee before its very first withdrawal can be processed.

automated_trading.notes: Apex's 'Prohibited Activities' policy bans 'AI, autobots, algorithms, fully-automated trading systems and software, high-frequency trading (HFT), and any other automated trading.' Tools that merely speed up manual order entry (hotkeys, bracket/OCO templates) are reported as permitted — the dividing line is full automation of entry/exit decisions, not trading-assistance tooling in general.

cross_account_hedging.notes: Apex states 'no hedging of any kind — directional trading only,' worded broadly enough to cover simultaneous opposing positions in the same/correlated instruments both within one account and across a trader's own multiple Apex accounts.

dca_or_martingale.notes: Not a flat ban: Apex's guidance targets martingale-style 'averaging into account death' as against the program's spirit, and a reported 2026-04 update permits at most one same-size re-entry on a losing trade, provided it doesn't trip the consistency rule. This is one of the most recently changed and least settled rules in Apex's book — re-confirm exact current wording before relying on it.

news_trading.notes: Trading through scheduled news/economic releases as part of an ordinary strategy is allowed; what Apex prohibits is 'chasing the market' or placing simultaneous opposing orders purely to gamble on a release's direction.

vpn_usage.notes: Apex bans VPNs, proxy servers, cloud servers and other anonymizing tools used 'for the purpose of misrepresenting, concealing, or disguising your identity, device, or location' — an identity/geography-integrity rule, not a blanket tooling ban.

copy_trading.notes: Copying/mirroring trades between DIFFERENT traders or accounts is prohibited, but Apex explicitly permits a trader to run one 'leader' account driving up to 19 'follower' accounts within their own Apex stable — consistent with Apex's stated cap of up to 20 active funded accounts per trader.

change_notes: Seed record compiled 2026-06-07 alongside this lineage's evaluation record — see that record's change_notes for sourcing caveats (official Apex pages returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; facts drawn from indexed snippets plus third-party corroboration). The headline figure here is the consistency cap, which is also the single biggest Legacy-vs-4.0 change Apex made: it moved from 30% of ALL-TIME cumulative profit (Legacy, grandfathered pre-2026-03-01 accounts) to 50% of profit SINCE THE LAST PAYOUT (current). Don't let an 'as of' query before 2026-03-01 resolve to this record — that date range needs its own Legacy-rule record, not yet in this knowledge base.

lock.notes: Same lock mechanic carries forward from evaluation into the PA: the EOD-trailing floor stops ratcheting and freezes at starting balance + $100 ($50,100 here) the first time the closing balance reaches that level, and never moves again afterward — even if the balance later falls back below it.

drawdown.notes: Identical mechanics to the evaluation phase (see that record): once-daily recalculation at 4:59:59 PM ET off the closing/realized balance. The consequence of a breach differs, though — in PA it triggers immediate account closure with open positions force-liquidated, vs. simply 'failing' an evaluation with nothing at stake but the entry fee.

consistency_rule.basis_definition: No single trading day's profit may equal or exceed 50% of the account's total net profit accumulated SINCE THE LAST APPROVED PAYOUT (or since account inception, if none yet). Equivalently, the minimum cumulative profit required to clear the gate = (largest single day's profit so far) / 0.5. This replaced Apex's prior Legacy formula — 30% of ALL-TIME cumulative profit — around 2026-03-01; note the denominator reset behavior (per-payout-cycle vs. all-time) is itself a material change, not just the percentage move from 30 to 50.
consistency_rule.violation_consequence: Does not fail the account or block trading day-to-day — it gates the payout request itself. A trader whose best day is too large a share simply cannot withdraw until additional, better-distributed profit brings the ratio back under the cap.

targets_and_days.notes: No ongoing profit target applies once funded — the PA only needs to stay above its drawdown floor. The figures shown here (5 days, $250/day net) are PAYOUT-gating requirements, not 'stay funded' requirements — see the payout block. The per-day minimum is reported to be account-size AND drawdown-variant specific: $250/day is the figure reported for a $50K EOD-trailing PA; the Intraday-trailing variant at the same size is reported to use $200/day. Confirm both numbers before marking this record 'verified'.

payout.eligibility_notes: Every payout request — first and subsequent — requires (a) at least 5 'qualifying' trading days (need not be consecutive) that each net at least the min_qualifying_day_amount shown alongside, AND (b) the consistency check above passing for profit accrued since the last payout. Separately, a one-time PA activation fee (reported in the ~$85-130 range, due within 7 days of passing the evaluation) must be paid before the very first withdrawal can be processed at all — activation_fee captures a $100 midpoint estimate pending confirmation of the exact figure.
payout.cadence_notes: Payouts can be requested on demand once the eligibility gates clear, but each PA carries a LIFETIME CAP of 6 total payouts, after which the PA is closed and the trader must requalify through a brand-new evaluation. Apex is reported to run a graduated payout-amount ladder across those 6 requests rather than a flat per-request ceiling (e.g. a $50K EOD PA reportedly steps from roughly $1,500 up toward $3,000 across the six, totaling near $13,000 lifetime); max_amount above captures only the FIRST-payout step of that ladder. The full per-step schedule is not yet modeled as structured data — needs direct verification and likely a future schema note (or per-payout-number records) to represent properly.

automated_trading.notes: Same firm-wide 'Prohibited Activities' policy as the evaluation phase carries into the PA unchanged — see that record. If anything, enforcement is reported to be stricter once real payouts are at stake, though the written rule itself does not differ by phase.

cross_account_hedging.notes: Same firm-wide 'no hedging of any kind — directional trading only' policy as the evaluation phase, applying across the trader's own multiple PAs as well as within a single account.

dca_or_martingale.notes: Same nuanced policy as the evaluation phase (see that record): discouraged as against the program's spirit, with a reported 2026-04 update allowing at most one same-size loser re-entry subject to the consistency rule. Re-confirm current wording specifically for funded-stage enforcement before relying on it.

news_trading.notes: Same policy as the evaluation phase: trading through news as part of an ordinary strategy is fine; placing opposing same-instant orders purely to gamble on a release's direction is not.

vpn_usage.notes: Same firm-wide identity/geography-integrity rule as the evaluation phase — VPNs, proxies, and other anonymizers used to misrepresent identity, device, or location remain banned once funded.

copy_trading.notes: Same policy as the evaluation phase: copying between different traders is banned, but running one 'leader' PA to drive up to 19 'follower' PAs within the trader's own Apex stable (cap: 20 active funded accounts total) is explicitly permitted — and is, in fact, the primary use case Apex's funded-stage copy-trading allowance exists to serve.
